Typed decisions for agents and workflows, in one forward pass, on your own machine.
Text, images, audio and video. 73k tokens of context. Calibrated probabilities, and an honest "I should not decide".

Quickstart · Docs · Benchmarks · Demo · Colab

> **Cite this work.** M, N.; M, A. From Laya to Vega: Open Non-Autoregressive Decision Models with Calibrated Probabilities. *Preprints* **2026**, 2026110781. [https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202611.0781.v1](https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202611.0781.v1)
BibTeX ```bibtex @article{m2026laya_vega, title = {From Laya to Vega: Open Non-Autoregressive Decision Models with Calibrated Probabilities}, author = {M, N. and M, A.}, journal = {Preprints}, year = {2026}, pages = {2026110781}, doi = {10.20944/preprints202611.0781.v1}, url = {https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202611.0781.v1} } ```

```bash pip install -U laya ``` ```python import laya agent = laya.Agent() out = agent.predict("We were billed twice for March. Refund it today or we cancel.", {"department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?", "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, refunds", "technical": "bugs, outages"}}}) out["answers"]["department"]["choice"] # 'billing', with probabilities, a prediction set and abstain ``` Python 3.10 or newer. Optional extras (HTTP server, MCP, LangChain, ONNX, images, audio), `uv`, GPU builds and per-platform steps are in [Installation details](#installation-details). ## What it does - **Text, images, audio and video.** `agent.predict(...)` with `image=`, `audio=` or `video=` gives the same typed answers as for text. - **73,728 tokens of context.** Whole contracts, threads and logs in one read. - **Abstain and unbound**, explained below. - **Physics, not text generation.** Each candidate answer is a valley; the input is a particle that rolls and settles in one. Deterministic, constant cost, nothing generated. - **Any LLM as the reader.** One small decision engine on top of a frozen reader, from 0.8B to 27B. - **Continuous learning** (`pip install vegaml-learn`, noncommercial licence, see the note below). `from laya import Learner`: it answers from day one and learns from every answer your team confirms, on your own machine, in seconds on a CPU with no fine-tuning. - **A teacher for what it is unsure of.** `laya.Escalator(learner, teacher)` sends only the records it abstains on, finds unbound or is not yet sure of to your teacher (a review queue, a rules engine, or a model you serve yourself with `laya.vllm_teacher`), serves that answer and learns from it, so the teacher is needed less and less. [Guide](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/docs/vegaml.md#a-teacher-for-what-it-is-unsure-of). > [!IMPORTANT] > **laya is Apache 2.0, free for any use. Continuous learning is not.** `laya.Learner`, `laya.Escalator` and `laya.vllm_teacher` need the separate package `vegaml-learn`, which is **noncommercial only** (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0). Research, study, personal projects, charities, schools and government are free. Using it in a company, a product or a paid service needs a commercial licence: [embedding.in/licence](https://embedding.in/licence), or write to [nandakishor@embedding.in](mailto:nandakishor@embedding.in). Everything else in laya is unaffected. ### How abstain and unbound work The input is placed as a particle in a small decision space where every candidate answer is a valley. Where the particle settles, and how deep, is the answer and its probability. - **`abstain`**: it declines to commit. The threshold is calibrated so that, among the answers it does give, the error rate stays under the configured risk (10% by default). - **`prediction_set`**: the conformal set, every option the answer could still be at `alpha` 0.10. One option means it is sure; two or more means the input really is ambiguous. - **`unbound`**: the particle settled far from every valley, so the input looks unlike anything it knows (likely off-distribution). It is reported on every answer but does not route on its own: measured, it also fired on 71% of normal banking77 rows, so it would have sent most good answers to review. - **`route`**: what to do with it, `auto` or `review`. Without labels, `review` when it abstains or the set holds more than one option. With labels (`agent.fit` / `agent.calibrate`), a band placed where precision holds at 95% on your rows decides. Gate on `route`, never on a confidence number. ### Benchmarks at a glance **Continuous learning.** 14 decision templates (31 questions), each starting from about 600 generated examples, then learning from confirmed answers; scored on 60 held-out rows per template. | | day one | after 40 confirmed answers | after 120 | |---|---|---|---| | laya, `laya.Learner` | 84.7% | 91.6% | **96.0%** | | Jev 1.14, confirmed answers written into its criteria | **89.5%** | 91.5% | 92.6% | Jev leads on day one (23 of 31 questions); they are level at 40; laya leads at 120 (12 wins, 7 losses, 12 ties). Jev cannot be taught, only prompted, and is a hosted API (364 ms a request from India). **What learning costs.** laya learns from 300 answers in 34 s on 8 CPU threads, with no GPU (0.72 s an answer, 6.4 GB of RAM; on a GPU 40 ms and 2 GB). Fine-tuning the classic encoder on the same 300 rows takes 89 s on a GPU with 9 GB and rewrites all 421M weights. **Learning from a stream, November 2026** (4B reader, held-out rows): | | laya | Jev 1.14 | |---|---|---| | banking77, 924 held out, after 4,928 rows | **87.5%**, ECE 0.028, 92.5% routed auto at 91.5% precision | 79.4% as shipped (ECE 0.078), 85.7% with examples | | typed-decisions, 2,000 decisions, after 1,200 rows | 73.7%, ECE **0.031** | 74.7%, ECE 0.047 (level) | **Across readers**, one byte-identical decision engine, 50,676 held-out records: 0.8B 76.5%, 4B 79.1%, 27B 81.1%, ECE 0.010 to 0.021. **Where it loses.** Zero-shot on generic public suites a large hosted model leads. As a prompt-injection gate on real traffic (ToxicChat, 1.8% attacks), Jev untaught catches 79.1% at 0.3% refused against 73.0% at 0.7% for a fitted head. The benchmarks further down are for the classic encoder checkpoints. Under the hood the new engine comes from [vegaml](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/vegaml), installed with laya. For the classic encoder, name it (`laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya")`) or pass `vegaml=False`. > **[Studio, from Embedding Space](https://studio.embedding.in)** builds the starting set for your questions and runs it for you. **Multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine.** Typed decisions over 100+ languages in a single forward pass — 33 ms — trained with reinforcement learning against strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD), with a router that picks the right checkpoint per request. ## Quickstart Since 0.5.0 `laya.Agent()` loads laya's new engine: a frozen 0.8B reader with a small physics engine on top, so every answer carries a conformal prediction set, an abstain flag, an out-of-distribution flag and a route decided without a threshold you had to guess at. Text, images, speech and 73k-token documents go through the same call. Python 3.10 or newer; details in [vega inside laya](#vega-inside-laya-agentvegamltrue). ```python import laya agent = laya.Agent() # the new engine with a 0.8B reader, the default since 0.5.0 # Switching the model underneath is one string. Every option keeps the same engine, questions and fields: # laya.Agent(vegaml="4b") # the Qwen3.5-4B reader from the same Hub repo # laya.Agent(vegaml="gemma-1b") # the gemma-3-1b-it reader, same repo # laya.Agent(vegaml="nandakishorm/vega-U") # any Hub repo id holding a vega-U checkpoint # laya.Agent(vegaml="./my-reader/") # a local dir from VegaAgent.attach(...), your own LLM ported in # laya.Agent(vegaml=True, backbone="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B") # name the reader weights explicitly, e.g. a mirror # Naming one of laya's own encoders loads it instead (or pass vegaml=False): # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya") # English, 33 ms on a T4 # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya-multilingual") # 100+ languages, up to 8,192 tokens with max_len=8192 # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya-typed-decisions") # fine-tuned for the typed-decisions workflows state = "Hi, we were billed twice for March. Please refund the duplicate today or we will cancel our plan." questions = { "department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?", "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds", "technical": "bugs, outages, system errors", "other": "everything else"}}, "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How urgent is this?", "criteria": ["not urgent", "soon", "blocking"]}, "churn_risk": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the user threaten to cancel or leave?"}, } out = agent.predict(state, questions) ans = out["answers"]["department"] print(ans["choice"]) # billing print(ans["probabilities"]) # {"billing": 0.91, "technical": 0.04, "other": 0.05} print(ans["prediction_set"]) # ["billing"]: the options the answer could still be, at alpha 0.1 print(ans["abstain"]) # False: the engine is not refusing this one print(ans["unbound"]) # False: the state looks like something it has seen (reported, never routes) print(ans["route"]) # "auto"; "review" when the engine abstains or the set holds more than one print(out["answers"]["churn_risk"]["noul"]) # probability the answer is yes ``` The output keeps laya's shape (`choice`, `score`, `noul`, `probabilities`, `answer_confidence`) and adds vega's fields. Gate on `route`, not on a confidence number: it comes from the conformal set and the fitted band, which stay right on answers where the top probability does not. **Model switching.** Keep a laya encoder for short English text and let vega take the rest: ```python from laya.vega import Router router = Router(fast=laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya"), vega=agent) out = router.predict(state, questions) print(out["routing"]) # {"model": "fast", "reason": "short English text, no fitted head: the fast encoder is enough"} out = router.predict("मुझसे मार्च में दो बार शुल्क लिया गया, कृपया डुप्लिकेट राशि वापस करें।", questions) print(out["routing"]["model"]) # vega: non-English goes to the reader ``` The rule, in order: an image or audio goes to vega; text longer than the fast model's context goes to vega; non-English or non-Latin text goes to vega; a question with a fitted head goes to vega; everything else goes to the encoder. `model="vega"` or `model="fast"` forces one. **Images, speech, video, long documents.** The questions and the answer shape do not change with the input: ```python # text: up to 73,728 tokens in one pass; usage["truncated"] says if a state hit the limit agent.predict_long(seventy_page_contract, questions) # image: PIL image, path or HxWx3 array, any format Pillow opens; scaled to ~1 megapixel, no file-size cap # needs pip install 'laya[vision]' (Pillow and torchvision), as does video agent.predict(image="invoice.png", questions=questions) # audio: path or bytes (wav, flac, ogg, mp3; needs pip install 'laya[audio]') or a 1-D waveform with sampling_rate=; # any length, resampled to 16 kHz, transcribed in 30 s windows, transcript counts toward the 73,728 tokens agent.predict(audio=wave, questions=questions, sampling_rate=16000) # video: path or bytes, any container ffmpeg opens, any length and resolution (needs the ffmpeg binary); # speech is transcribed and decided as text, a silent clip is decided on 4 sampled frames as one image agent.predict(video="call.mp4", questions=questions) ``` **Fit and calibrate on your own labels.** Seconds, no gradient step, and the route is decided for you. Labels are a CSV with a `state` column and one column per question id; [`examples/data/routing_labels.csv`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/examples/data/routing_labels.csv) is a 60-row example that routes messages to billing, HR, PR, sales or technical and rates their urgency: ```csv state,team,urgency "We were charged twice for the March invoice, please refund the duplicate.",billing,2 "I would like to apply for the open backend engineer role. Where do I send my CV?",hr,0 "A journalist from the Economic Times is asking for a comment on today's outage.",pr,2 ``` The whole loop, from import to the answer, is [`examples/42_fit_and_calibrate_vegaml.py`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/examples/42_fit_and_calibrate_vegaml.py). It holds out 4 rows per team (20), fits on the other 40, and measures the same 20 rows before and after. Condensed: ```python import csv, laya questions = { "team": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team should handle this message?", "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds", "hr": "jobs, payroll, leave, policy", "pr": "press, media, public statements", "sales": "pricing, demos, quotes, trials", "technical": "bugs, outages, API and product questions"}}, "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How soon does this need a reply?", "criteria": ["can wait", "this week", "today"]}, } rows = list(csv.DictReader(open("examples/data/routing_labels.csv"))) held, fit_rows = rows[-20:], rows[:-20] # the script holds out 4 per team; same idea agent = laya.Agent(vegaml=True) print(laya.VegaAgent.min_rows(questions)) # 35: the fewest rows fit() accepts for these questions before = agent.predict(held[0]["state"], questions)["answers"]["team"] # the cold engine report = agent.fit([{"state": r["state"], "gold": {"team": r["team"], "urgency": r["urgency"]}} for r in fit_rows], questions=questions) # or agent.fit("examples/data/routing_labels.csv", questions=questions) print(report["n_fit"], report["n_calibrate"]) # 30 fit the heads, 10 are held out inside fit() to calibrate on print(report["serving"]) # the questions whose head beat the engine on the same rows print(report["calibration"]["band"]) # the review line per question, or None where it could not hold after = agent.predict(held[0]["state"], questions)["answers"]["team"] agent.save_calibration("fit-routing/") # heads + calibration; agent.load_calibration("fit-routing/") later ``` What the script printed on a laptop GPU, every number measured in that run: ``` minimum rows fit() accepts for these questions: 35 (5 per option of the widest question for the heads, plus a quarter held out to calibrate on, never fewer than 10) == before: the cold engine, 20 held-out rows team accuracy 0.600 ECE 0.221 mean confidence 0.629 urgency accuracy 0.400 ECE 0.412 MAE 0.65 levels team set sizes {1: 13, 2: 7} abstain 12 route {'auto': 6, 'review': 14} == fit + calibrate on 40 rows in 9s: 30 fit the heads, 10 held out to calibrate on team head cv 0.767 vs engine 0.633 on the same rows -> SERVED urgency head cv 0.400 vs engine 0.400 on the same rows -> left to the engine team temperature 0.83 conformal q-hat 0.987 ECE on the calibration rows 0.281 -> 0.241 urgency temperature 6.44 conformal q-hat 0.741 ECE on the calibration rows 0.515 -> 0.142 review line per question: {'team': None, 'urgency': None} ['team', 'urgency']: no line holds precision 0.95 with a 95% bound on 10 calibration rows, so the conformal set routes those answers == after: heads + calibration, 20 held-out rows team accuracy 0.900 ECE 0.206 mean confidence 0.749 urgency accuracy 0.400 ECE 0.059 MAE 0.65 levels team set sizes {2: 2, 3: 2, 4: 6, 5: 10} abstain 0 route {'
